title: Bias-weighted bidirectional LSTM toxicity classifier
summary: The solution tokenizes lowercased comment text with a regex, truncates to 220 tokens, and builds a training-derived vocabulary retaining tokens with frequency at least five, capped at 200,000; other tokens map to unknown. A learned embedding with spatial dropout feeds two stacked bidirectional LSTMs. Masked temporal max and mean pooling are concatenated, processed by two ReLU dense layers with a residual connection, and projected to one toxicity logit plus identity auxiliary logits. Training uses weighted binary cross-entropy for toxicity and unweighted binary cross-entropy for identity labels. Identity-mentioning rows and selected toxic/non-toxic background/subgroup cases receive increased toxicity loss weights, normalized by mean weight. Length-bucketed shuffled batches reduce padding. Adam optimization uses mixed-precision gradient scaling, gradient-norm clipping, and exponential learning-rate decay after each of four epochs. Validation inference batches padded sequences, applies sigmoid to the toxicity logit, and evaluates continuous probabilities.
